subject: Capacity-plus upgrade path and soft fallback plan
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@shoply.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 10:15:00 -0400
Subject: Capacity-plus upgrade path and soft fallback plan

Hi Oliver —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I put together a short proposal for Shoply's hosted API renewal + a staged commit uplift so you have runway during Q4 holiday traffic. Key points: 

- Monthly commit: move from current 800M tokens/month to 1.6B tokens/month (2x) for an initial 3-month term.
- Rate limits: primary lane at 400 requests/min with an optional burst lane (1,000 r/min) subject to soft-fallback rules.
- Soft fallback: automatic fallback to the 1.0B commit variant if sustained burst exceeds the buffer for >10 minutes; we will notify via email + Console alerting.
- Billing: monthly invoices pro-rated for the first period; standard 30-day net payment.

Attached is a redline-friendly SOW and your usage export for May–July so we can validate the sizing. If Shoply confirms procurement contact and PO timing, we can prepare the DocuSign package and routing.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm procurement contact and PO ETA (Oliver / procurement@shoply.com)
2) Review SOW and send any redlines by EOD Thu (9/16)
3) If accepted, we’ll send DocuSign and target the uplift to begin on 10/1/2027

Attached: SOW_Shoply_v2.pdf (redline-enabled), shoply_usage_May-July2027.csv

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi

Irene — thanks for the note and the materials. A couple quick items from our side after running the numbers: 

- Can you confirm exact per-token unit pricing at the 1.6B commit level, and whether there are stepped discounts above 2B? We need this for our internal finance approval.
- Rate limit behaviour: what happens to in-flight requests during the soft fallback (timeouts, retries)? We want to avoid user-visible failures during checkout spikes.
- Billing cadence: we prefer quarterly invoicing for large commits; is that an option or do you require monthly?

Procurement here is cc’d (procurement@shoply.com) — they’ll need a final SOW and the DocuSign link. Please mark the SOW as redline-friendly; we usually return it with a handful of legal comments.

If you can share a short ops note describing the fallback behaviour and retry guidance we can send to our engineers. Otherwise this looks like the right path.

—Oliver

Folks — internal ops note and suggested SOW updates for Shoply (per Oliver's questions):

Summary of recommendations:
- Pricing: 
  - Base unit price at 1.6B commit: $0.0012 per token (list) with a staged discount to $0.00105 above 2.0B.
  - Include a one-time onboarding credit of $15k if they sign by 9/24 (helps close).
- Rate limits and fallback behaviour:
  - During soft fallback we will route new requests to the 1.0B commit model variant and honor existing in-flight KV caches for 30s; requests beyond that are rejected with 429 and a Retry-After header.
  - Recommend we provision a short-lived burst buffer (1,000 r/min) enforced for <10 minutes; after that period automatic fallback to lower commit. Console alert and email escalation to their on-call.
- Billing cadence: we can do quarterly invoicing for committed deals above $200k ARR; otherwise default monthly. Shoply is close to the threshold; request procurement to confirm PO timing.

Action items (Irene):
- Update SOW with pricing table and the ops fallback note (attached).
- Generate DocuSign package and copy procurement@shoply.com into envelope.
- Karthik to confirm that soft-fallback behaviour will not invalidate SLA for their Dedicated customers (he confirmed on call that Hosted SLOs remain intact).

Attached: SOW_Shoply_v2.pdf (redlines inline)

Vanessa Ortiz
